headline: Full Stack Developer & Gardener · Example Account
bio: This is an example profile to show what the Project Library looks like with real content. Sam is a fictional software engineer and vegetable gardener based in Berkeley who volunteers teaching coding fundamentals.
aboutContent:
👋 This is an example account created to demonstrate how the Project Library works. Sam Example is a fictional person.

I've been writing software for about eight years, mostly full-stack web work with React, Node, and PostgreSQL. Before that I studied computer science and worked in civic tech.

Outside of work I maintain a fairly ambitious backyard garden — raised beds, a small greenhouse, and more tomato varieties than any reasonable person needs. I like the overlap between debugging code and debugging why my basil keeps bolting.

I volunteer with a local group that teaches coding fundamentals to people making career changes.

posts.title: Raised Bed Garden Build (Example Post)
posts.content:
📌 This is an example post showing what project updates look like on the Project Library.

Built three new raised beds this spring using cedar planks. Each one is 4x8 feet, filled with a mix of compost, peat moss, and vermiculite. Already planted tomatoes, peppers, basil, and a few experimental squash varieties.

The cedar should last 10-15 years without treatment, and the height makes weeding much easier on the back.

updates.title: First harvest (example update)
updates.content: 📌 Example update post. The basil and lettuce are producing way more than I can eat. Gave a big bag of each to my neighbor. Tomatoes are still green but sizing up nicely — another few weeks.

posts.title: Building Accessible Component Libraries (Example Post)
posts.content:
📌 This is an example post.

Notes from a talk I gave at our local meetup about building React component libraries with accessibility baked in from the start.

Key takeaways: use semantic HTML before reaching for ARIA, test with a screen reader during development (not after), and make keyboard navigation a first-class concern in every interactive component.
